text:
Situation: Dopamine hydrochloride injection remains on FDA's shortage list as Current. Baxter Healthcare shows an initial posting date of 2017-11-06 and an update date of 2026-10-16. Hospira, Inc. shows an initial posting date of 2017-11-06 and an update date of 2026-10-08. As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has been listed for 108 months. Current on-hand supply across Corvale sites ranges from 11.7 to 13.8 days at present usage rates.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list records dopamine hydrochloride injection as Current for both Baxter Healthcare and Hospira, Inc., with the initial posting date of 2017-11-06 and the most recent updates on 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-08 respectively.

Our position: We have two P&T-approved alternate manufacturers for dopamine hydrochloride 40 mg/mL. Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. was approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD on 2025-10-24. Hospira, Inc. was approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD on 2025-12-19. Both require dose and volume recalculation and pharmacist verification. FDA lists both products as Current with initial posting dates of 2017-11-06.

Recommended actions:
1. Procure dopamine hydrochloride 40 mg/mL from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. as primary alternate; requires pharmacist verification at dispensing. Approval: P&T Committee.
2. Procure dopamine hydrochloride 40 mg/mL from Hospira, Inc. as secondary alternate; requires pharmacist verification at dispensing. Approval: P&T Committee.
3. Implement daily inventory monitoring across all Corvale sites with alerts when any site falls below 10 days' supply. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
4. Communicate alternate product availability and recalculation requirements to all clinical pharmacists. Approval: Clinical Pharmacy Manager.

Not recommended: Switching to non-formulary vasopressors without P&T review; purchasing from non-approved manufacturers; altering dosing protocols without clinician and committee authorization.
